items.title: 68356_Howard R. Scott oral history interview
items.q: And they were short a trumpet player one time, and Cecil told him, said, Casco, why don't you get Scotty? He knows all the popular tunes, he could play.

ctx.x: Oh, yes, yeah, all that was extra, sure. A lot of recordings. In this respect, I had been playing before then mostly popular music. And we had to make a lot of music that was more on the blues side.

Now, one time, when I was working with them, I played for the fellow, W.C. Handy, that wrote the St. Louis Blues. These fellows that had come out of the Army -- and they all belonged to the Amsterdam, a guy by the name of Casco Williams, the saxophone player. He and Cecil knew each other, they had been in the band together, Jim Mueller's band. And they were short a trumpet player one time, and Cecil told him, said, Casco, why don't you get Scotty? He knows all the popular tunes, he could play.

They got me, and I was scared to death. Old Man Handy was on the job. We played down on Fifth Avenue in a millionaires house, because those days, there was nothing but millionaires that owned the places there. They hadn't torn them all down
